column1: # service-registry.tsv — the DECLARATIVE single source of every key service the fleet
# supervises. generate-monit-config.sh renders monit.d/*.conf FROM this file (never hand-edit
# monit config); discover-services.sh evaluates it (monit-independent) and fails-closed on any
# running critical service NOT listed here. Adding a row here == that service is monitored on the
# next render + evaluation. See fleet/board/SERVICE-LIVENESS-WATCHDOG.md and fleet/watchdog/.
# ROOT INCIDENT this closes: the OOB grader-daemon (sole writer of model-scorecard.tsv) died on a
# reboot with NO supervisor and never restarted, silently killing grade->route for 9 days. A HUNG
# service that produces nothing must alarm exactly like a DEAD one -> hence the freshness columns.
# COLUMNS (TAB-separated, exactly 7). Grammar lives in fleet/watchdog/watchdog-lib.sh:
#   name             stable id (monit-safe)
#   kind             process | host | socket | file (informational; the probe strings are canonical)
#   alive_probe      pgrep:<ere> | pidfile:<path> | tcp:<host>:<port> | unixsock:<path> | program:<cmd> | none
#   freshness_probe  file:<path> | none      (a HUNG-but-alive service is caught here)
#   freshness_ttl_s  integer seconds; freshness_probe mtime must be within this window (0 when none)
#   restart_cmd      command monit runs to restart it (seed values — operator confirms per box)
#   owner            who owns the service
# restart_cmd CONTRACT (WATCHDOG-RESTART-CMDS-VERIFY, 2026-07-24) — every value in column 6 is run
# by monit as ROOT, with cwd=/ and no login shell/PATH/agent. The four seed values were all written
# from a `stack` interactive-shell viewpoint and were BROKEN in that context (no such systemd unit /
# `systemctl --user` as root / a relative path to a missing file / a ~/.ssh/config Host alias root
# cannot see + a remote sudo with no NOPASSWD). Enabling monit with those meant: service dies ->
# monit runs a failing command -> auto-recovery misfires. So column 6 now obeys:
#   - absolute paths for EVERY command word (no PATH, no cwd)
#   - no ~ / $HOME (root's ~ is /root), no `systemctl --user`, no sudo
#   - no ' or " (generate-monit-config.sh renders it inside /bin/sh -c '<cmd>')
#   - a non-root service is entered with `runuser -u <user> --`, and detached (`setsid ... &`) so
#     monit's `start program ... with timeout 60 seconds` is not blocked by a foreground daemon
#   - the ssh leg pins -i <key>, BatchMode=yes and UserKnownHostsFile (root has none of stack's)
# fleet/watchdog/verify-restart-cmds.sh ENFORCES all of the above and must be GREEN before anyone
# runs `systemctl enable --now monit`; monit-selfwatch.sh refuses to print the enable step until it is.
# SEED NOTES (confirmed on the live box 2026-07-24, restart_cmds corrected):
#   grader-daemon  process is fleet/benchmark/grader-daemon.py (runs as unix user bench-grader,
#                  whose shell is /usr/sbin/nologin — hence `runuser -u`, never `su -l`). The seed
#                  `systemctl restart bench-grader-daemon` named a unit that does NOT exist; the
#                  live launch is bench-grader-setup.sh's `setsid nohup python3 ...`, which column 6
#                  now reproduces verbatim under root. A real unit is SHIPPED (not installed) at
#                  fleet/watchdog/units/bench-grader-daemon.service — see that dir's README.
#                  freshness = the live scorecard mtime (fleet/model-scorecard.tsv on the MAIN
#                  checkout ~/charon-private). TTL 5400s (~3 write-cycles slack) catches a dead
#                  grader (the 9-day incident) without false-alarming a normal ~30-min write gap.
#   session-bridge process is ~/.config/opencode/session-bridge/proxy.py. freshness is `none` for
#                  now: the sqlite is WAL-mode and the -wal mtime is a NOISY signal (checkpoint
#                  truncation + low write traffic false-alarm a HEALTHY bridge). TODO: replace with
#                  a real lease/heartbeat-row freshness probe once one is exposed as a file/endpoint.
#   gateway-4lom   remote on 4-LOM (10.0.1.60:8080). VERIFIED: charon-gateway is a DOCKER container
#                  (`charon-gateway-1`), NOT a systemd unit, and the remote `stack` has NO NOPASSWD
#                  sudo — so the seed `ssh 4-LOM sudo systemctl restart charon-gateway` was wrong
#                  three ways. Restart is `docker restart charon-gateway-1` over an explicitly
#                  keyed, BatchMode ssh (stack is in the remote docker group).
#   roci-tunnel    the coordinator socket; existence == the SSH tunnel is up. The real reconnect
#                  script is ~/.charon/ensure-coordinator-tunnel.sh (idempotent, self-detaching);
#                  the seed pointed at fleet/bridge-reconnect.sh, which has never existed.
# name
grader-daemon
session-bridge
gateway-4lom
column6: /usr/bin/ssh -i /home/stack/.ssh/4lom -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10 -o UserKnownHostsFile=/home/stack/.ssh/known_hosts -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes stack@10.0.1.60 docker restart charon-gateway-1
